method: Browsed stronger search coverage and accessible classical translation/practitioner documents; kept classical attribution separate from later applications. No copied paragraphs, invented verses, outcome guarantees or named-person anecdotes. Examples and workflows are original.

sources.work: Brihat Parashara Hora Shastra, available English text PDF; translator/edition not securely established from this file
supports: D4 uses four quarters mapped through the four kendras of the source sign.
D10 uses ten 3-degree parts, starting at the source sign when odd and its ninth when even.
D4 is assigned fortunes; D10 power and position. The article distinguishes later property/career applications.
sources.limitations: The accessible electronic text contains editorial/transcription errors elsewhere. No invented Sanskrit verse or verbatim passage is reproduced. Only the specified checked rules are used. The separate horasad PDF search result returned 404 and was not used.

sources.work: P. V. R. Narasimha Rao, Lessons on Vedic Astrology, Volume I, student compilation, 2005
supports: Documented practitioner teaching of D10 calculation and comparison with rasi.
sources.limitations: Student summaries, not a classical primary text. The lesson does not reproduce practitioner anecdotes or charts and does not use the stronger deterministic claims found elsewhere in the compilation.

sources.work: P. V. R. Narasimha Rao, Lessons on Vedic Astrology, Volume II, student compilation, 2007
supports: Documents D4 as a property-focused practitioner method and distinguishes comfort from property-related expenditure.
sources.limitations: Used to attribute modern/practitioner property application, rather than claiming all detailed rules occur in BPHS. Existing individual examples and their claimed outcomes are not reused.

supports: Documents more than one D4 variation, supporting a settings check.
Documents separate transit calculations from natal Moon and lagna and searches near natal longitudes.
sources.limitations: Software capability is evidence for available calculations, not scientific validation of predicted outcomes.

sources.work: Mantreswara, Phaladeepika, chapter 26, V. Subrahmanya Sastri translation, 1950
supports: Moon-centered transit rules must retain their stated reference.
Jupiter in second/ninth from natal Moon appears in the general favorable list; the full qualification is not reduced to one placement.
The chapter includes vedha qualifications; a chart missing other transit planets cannot be described as fully checked.
sources.limitations: Wisdomlib warns that text OCR is not proofread. No original Sanskrit transcription is used; no purported verbatim quote. Lagna-based life-area workflow is explicitly the article teaching approach, not attributed to opening verse.
